title: Deepfakes, AI Scams and Synthetic Reality
description: Deepfakes, fake voices, synthetic images and AI-written scams are changing how people judge what is real online. This plain-English guide explains the problem without resorting to panic theatre. Deepfakes, AI Scams and Synthetic Reality shows how artificial intelligence can be used to imitate people, manipulate media, scale fraud, fake authority and erode trust. It also explains what readers can do about it. Written for general readers, small business owners, professionals, managers, families, creators and community leaders, the book covers practical warning signs, verification habits, safer communication rules, business procedures, social media judgement and the emotional tricks behind scams. It avoids invented statistics and horror imagery. The aim is simple: help readers become harder to fool. The answer is not to distrust everything. That way lies madness and terrible group chats. The answer is to slow down, verify better, protect identity, set rules for money and sensitive requests, and understand how synthetic media changes the trust game.
short_description: A calm guide to deepfakes, AI scams, voice cloning and synthetic media, with practical verification habits for people and small organisations.
author: Jonathan Harris
audience: General readers, small business owners, managers, professionals, families, educators, creators and anyone concerned about online trust, fraud and synthetic media.
